scope: The eight src/apps/* CLI front-ends named as next by M35. Contract checks against OpenSSL 3.6.4 for argument-string lifetimes, file/BIO ownership on every exit, option-table bounds, error tails, allocation arithmetic, and getter-returned or body-owned raw pointers; genuine arithmetic, ownership and option-fallback defects repaired.
worktree: source: src/apps/{mac,ocsp,pkcs12}.rs repaired; src/apps/{keyio,nseq,passwd,pkcs7,pkcs8}.rs audited with no source change. queue/receipt: REMAINING-AUDIT.txt, AUDITED-FILES.txt, PERFILE-INDEX.md section 40 and this file.

reconciliation.method: AUDITED-FILES.txt is the union of each mechanism sweep's structured .files array, the M1 files, the structured per-file records and each boundary sweep's structured boundaries. The eight files added here were absent from the pre-batch file (verified with an anchored grep over AUDITED-FILES.txt before insertion) and were the first eight entries of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt.
reconciliation.difference_from_325: M35 left 325 audited / 438 unaudited. This batch moves the eight files it named as next; no skipped boundary was removed from the remaining queue.

file_dispositions.note: Every CString outlives its BIO_new_file/BIO_new_fp call, each BIO is released exactly once on every exit (including the load_pubkey failure re-open), and no decoder getter pointer escapes the call.

The OSSL_PARAM array used (sz + 1) * size_of unchecked, so the product could wrap before CRYPTO_zalloc and later params.add(i) writes. It now uses checked_add/checked_mul and returns NULL, matching OPENSSL_calloc's rejection (the same repair M35 made in kdf). app_params_free stops at the calloc'ed terminator; len <= BUFSIZE bounds the hex loop and BIO_write.

mechanisms: seq->certs stack ownership and OPENSSL_sk_* bounds
file_dispositions.note: seq is assigned on both arms before the common end:; the stack and its certificates are released once by NETSCAPE_CERT_SEQUENCE_free; every exit frees out before in as apps/nseq.c does.

The loaded issuer/cert and fetched cert_id_md were never released (apps/ocsp.c:900-911 frees all three), and a replaced -issuer/-cert leaked its predecessor. A documented OcspState single-owner Drop now releases them on every exit; -cert frees the previous certificate before loading its replacement as apps/ocsp.c:481 does. The detached OCSP_CERTID on an OCSP_request_add0_id failure remains unreleased, matching the authority's stack-only sk_OCSP_CERTID_free.

Every digest write fits its fixed buffer; passwd[..1] is reached only when the length is non-zero; md5 permutation indices stay below 16 and the SHA-256/512 tables below 32/64. Non-ASCII salts truncate by char rather than byte, and -in -/-stdin are unlanded: retained compatibility divergences, not memory-safety defects.

-iter fell back to 0 on a failed parse, silently selecting the default iteration count; opt_int_arg yields -1 on failure, which is now preserved. cert/key are released once on every path and after PKCS12_free, never before.

A failed d2i/PEM decode clears the out-slot through ASN1_item_ex_free, so the later PKCS7_free(p7) is not a double free; the stack walk is bounds-checked by OPENSSL_sk_num; all three resources are released once on every return.

pkey, p8inf, out and inbio are released once on every branch; the conversion routines do not transfer ownership. -iter/-saltlen are parsed but unused in the landed -nocrypt arms and only feed the unlanded encrypted arms.

defects.detail: (sz + 1) * size_of::<OsslParam>() could wrap before CRYPTO_zalloc; replaced with checked_add/checked_mul returning NULL.
issuer, certificate and fetched cert_id_md (and replaced issuer/cert) were never released; now owned by OcspState with one Drop.
-iter parse failure selected 0 (the default) instead of opt_int_arg's -1.

new_unsafe_assumptions.name: OcspState single-owner release
new_unsafe_assumptions.detail: Each field is NULL or the frame's single reference; Drop releases through OCSP_REQUEST_free/X509_free/EVP_MD_free, all of which accept NULL. EVP_MD_free is the authority's no-op for a static legacy method.
